To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Brillouin light-scattering measurements of the high-frequency elastic properties have shown that the Young's modulus of collagen in dry tendon is 12 GPa and that in wet collagen it decreases to 5 GPa.
the elastic properties (stiffness) of the collagen molecule are highly anisotropic.
the high-frequency (GHz) elastic constants of collagen have been determined by Brillouin (elastic) light scattering and the results are consistent with the molecular structure of this protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of Brillouin scattering spectroscopy as a technique for the investigation of the mechanical properties and molecular structure of biological systems.
the development of Brillouin scattering as a tool in the study of the mechanical properties, particularly the elastic properties, of fibrous protein materials.

the development of a new experimental technique for measuring the mechanical properties of materials and with the application of this technique to the determination of some of the mechanical properties, in particular the high-frequency elastic properties, of collagen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Brillouin scattering technique is a very powerful method of determining elastic constants in biological materials, but that the interpretation of the results in terms of molecular structure and function is not yet complete.

the high frequency elastic properties of fibrous proteins are determined primarily by the molecular structure and that the mechanical properties of the composite materials depend on the degree and type of cross-linking between the molecules.
the Brillouin scattering technique is a valuable method for studying the elastic properties of biological materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Brillouin light-scattering method can be applied to the study of fibrous proteins, but that it is only applicable to dry fibres, or to wet fibres in which the molecular conformation is such that the longitudinal branch is observed.

the elastic properties are determined by the molecular structure of the collagen molecule and that the mechanical properties of the collagen composite material are determined by the packing of the molecular units in the collagen fibre.
the elastic properties are determined by the molecular assembly, not the molecular structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Brillouin technique can be used to determine the high-frequency elastic properties, and therefore the molecular dynamics, of fibrous protein materials.
Brillouin light spectroscopy (BLS) is a useful tool for measuring the elastic constants of fibrous materials.
the Brillouin technique is a useful tool in the study of biological materials.
